process_contract.termination: Use timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s for every potentially blocking CLI command. Each Python/Node subprocess must have its own finite timeout. Network requests additionally need explicit request/connect/read deadlines and finite byte/request/retry limits. No servers, watch modes, stdin prompts, detached processes or unbounded polling.
process_contract.compute: Offline synthetic or already inspected data only in wave 1. One prospectively fixed inference candidate and one calibration run; do not tune/retry to obtain PASS. At most 90 seconds per candidate run, 120 seconds outer timeout. Save partial failure evidence and exit nonzero on budget exhaustion.
process_contract.ownership: Each agent edits only its explicitly assigned new files. Coordinator owns synthesis, plan, handoff, integration, commits, pushes and state changes. Agents do not spawn agents or modify shared evaluators/frozen protocols.
process_contract.status_delivery: Each specialist posts sources, exact commands, test results, accepted scope, limitations, and next prerequisite in its assigned issue. A reported blocker is a response, not agent loss.
process_contract.nonresponse: On an actually unanswered status request, wait at least 60 seconds before one retry; after a second 60-second unanswered interval inspect artifacts and owned processes, document both requests/observations and apply Lost Repeat only to that truly lost assignment. An unstarted/unavailable agent is blocked, not lost.
process_contract.review: Independent critic starts after all working agents deliver or are evidenced lost. Critic checks source provenance, methodology, bias, tests and acceptance claims; no automatic GitHub approval or whole-epic acceptance.
process_contract.publication: Validate targeted packages and integrated suite, reconcile docs and labels, commit with Copilot trailer, push without force to the existing draft PR branch, verify remote head and issue states. Never silently overwrite concurrent changes.
